## The symptom

`testing:run` invoked with `timeoutMs: 240000` on a genuinely slow test file returned an
MCP `-32001` ("Request timed out; the tool call may have executed — verify its state before
retrying") after **~30–36s** — not the 240s asked for, not even the tool's own documented
50s foreground ceiling. **No `runId` was delivered**, so the caller couldn't look up the run
that was, in fact, still executing server-side.

Reported independently by two different agents on the same day (EI-21106949380687332) — the
tell that this is a class bug, not a one-off flake.

## Root cause: two independently-chosen timeout budgets, in two different files

`testing:run` (and `build:typecheck`, `capability:bash`, `capability:inspect`, `code:run`) is
a **FOREGROUND-capable** tool. Per
`packages/operator-core/lib/agent-tools/capability/foreground-transport-cap.ts`:

- the MCP transport hard-caps a call at `MCP_TRANSPORT_CAP_MS` (~55s) — not the tool's to
  change;
- so every foreground-capable tool self-clamps its OWN command timeout to
  `FOREGROUND_TIMEOUT_CEILING_MS` (50s, 5s of margin below the transport cap) via
  `clampForegroundTimeoutMs()`, so the TOOL always self-times-out first and returns an
  actionable `{ error: 'timeout', runId, hint: 're-run detached' }` payload instead of being
  killed by the transport with an opaque error.

That is a well-designed, well-tested contract (`foreground-transport-cap.test.ts` pins it as
a class invariant). But it only covers the SERVER side. The CALLER here was `ptool`
(`apps/operator/scripts/ptool.mjs`), and ptool has its own, entirely separate,
**client**-side per-`tools/call` request deadline: `timeoutForTool(toolName, callArgs)`,
which fell through to the flat `PTOOL_CALL_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS` (**30s**) for any tool not
explicitly listed in `PTOOL_LONG_RUNNING_TIMEOUTS_MS` — regardless of the tool's own
`timeoutMs` **argument**, which only ever reaches the server handler.

So: caller passes `timeoutMs: 240000` → the tool clamps that down to 50s server-side →
ptool's client gives up and aborts the whole MCP request at 30s, before the server's
carefully-designed 50s self-timeout (or its success case) can ever be observed. The
handler's response — which already carries a `runId` on every branch, including the timeout
one — is discarded in flight. The caller sees a raw transport error and no way to find the
run that is still going.

## The invariant this violates (same shape as WI-6738 / `budgets.mjs`)

> **A client's request timeout MUST be >= the longest the thing it's calling can legitimately
> take, or the client's own patience is what actually governs the call — silently, and usually
> shorter than anyone intended.**

This is the *exact* pattern `apps/operator/lib/mcp-proxy/budgets.mjs` already documents for
psu vs the mcp-proxy retry window (a client timeout chosen independently of what it's
fronting drifts apart from it). It recurs here because `ptool.mjs` is a SEPARATE client with
its own independently-chosen timeout table, and nothing tied its per-tool entries to the set
of tools that self-clamp to `FOREGROUND_TIMEOUT_CEILING_MS`.

## The fix

`ptool.mjs`'s `PTOOL_LONG_RUNNING_TIMEOUTS_MS` map now carries every tool that imports and
calls `clampForegroundTimeoutMs` (`testing:run`, `build:typecheck`, `capability:bash`,
`capability:inspect`, `code:run`) mapped to `PTOOL_FOREGROUND_TOOL_TIMEOUT_MS` (60s — above
`MCP_TRANSPORT_CAP_MS` with real margin), instead of the flat 30s default. ptool.mjs is a
plain `.mjs` run under bare `node` (same constraint as `budgets.mjs`), so it can't import the
`.ts` constants directly — the coupling is documented in a comment at the definition site
instead, cross-referencing `foreground-transport-cap.ts` by name.

## If you add a new foreground-capable tool (a new `clampForegroundTimeoutMs` caller)

You must ALSO add it to `PTOOL_LONG_RUNNING_TIMEOUTS_MS` in `ptool.mjs`. Nothing enforces this
automatically today (unlike the server-side class guard in
`foreground-transport-cap.test.ts`, which enumerates every honourer as a hard-coded list and
fails if one is missing) — `ptool.test.ts`'s
`describe('ptool timeoutForTool — foreground-capable tools outlive the MCP transport cap')`
enumerates the same 5 tools by name and will need the new one added by hand. A future
tightening would derive both lists from one place instead of two hand-maintained arrays.

## Diagnosing a similar report

- Symptom: an MCP `-32001`/timeout on a tool that documents its own longer `timeoutMs`
  budget, arriving well BEFORE that budget elapses, with no `runId`/handle in the error.
- Check: is the CALLER `ptool`, or another thin MCP client with its own per-call deadline
  independent of the tool's argument? If so, check that client's own timeout table against
  the tool's actual server-side ceiling — the tool's `timeoutMs` ARGUMENT never controls the
  calling client's patience.
